title: Cookbook:Red Lentil Soup
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Soup recipes
| Servings = 4
| Image = [[File:Lentil soup in a bowl.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{recipe}}| [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|Vegan Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Soups|Soups]]

== Ingredients ==
* 1–2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrots]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 2 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] dry red [[Cookbook:Lentil|lentils]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] water or [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaf]]

== Procedure ==
#[[File:Lentil soup done.jpg|thumb|Finished lentil soup, with potatoes, parsley, and dill added|308x308px]]Pick over the lentils to remove any debris if needed. Rinse well.
#Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Once oil is hot, add the onion and carrots. [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] for a few minutes, until the vegetables have started to soften, then add the garlic.
#Add the lentils, bay leaf, and water to the pot. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] over low-medium heat for 20–30 minutes until lentils are softened. 
#Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Herbs and/or spices can be added to the sautéing vegetables, such as [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]], [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]], [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]], and/or [[Cookbook:Red Pepper|red pepper]] flakes.  
* [[Cookbook:Hot Sauce|Hot sauce]] can be added to taste. Freshly-squeezed [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]] is a nice addition, preferably immediately before serving.

title: Cookbook:Basic Scrambled Eggs
text:
__NOTOC__{{Recipe summary
| Category = Egg recipes
| Servings = 1
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}}

== Ingredients ==
* 3 [[Cookbook:egg|egg]]s
* 2–3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] (optional)
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] (or to taste)
* ⅛ tsp [[Cookbook:pepper|black pepper]] (or to taste)

== Procedure ==
# Crack eggs into a measuring cup.
# Add the milk (if desired) and salt.
# Using a [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] or fork, [[Cookbook:Beating|beat]] the mixture until foamy.
# Melt butter in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] on medium heat
# Pour eggs into frying pan.
# Stir mixture to break up the egg as it cooks and allow more liquid to touch the hot pan. Stirring rapidly will create small curds, while slower stirring will create larger curds.
# Cook until just before you feel that they are done, since the eggs will continue to cook after being removed from the pan. The eggs are done when the sheen disappears; stop cooking just before this happens.
# Transfer to a plate. Season with black pepper (black pepper will burn and become bitter if seasoned before cooking).
# Eat as is or with [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]] ([[Cookbook:Tomato Sauce|tomato sauce]]), [[Cookbook:Salsa|salsa]], and/or butter on [[Cookbook:Toast|toast]].

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* For a [[Cookbook:Low-sodium Cooking|low-sodium]] version, omit salt and use unsalted butter.
* Grated [[Cookbook:Cheddar cheese|cheddar cheese]] can be added into the mixture or on top of the cooked eggs.
* Sour cream may be used in place of milk for a creamier and richer version.
* Cook ⅓ cup (25 g / 0.88 oz) of crumbled cooked meats (like [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]] or [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]]) or chopped vegetables (like [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]] or [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]]) for a couple of minutes before adding the egg mixture. See also [[Cookbook:Southwestern Scramble|Southwestern Scramble]].

title: Cookbook:Oat Porridge
text:
{{recipesummary|category=Breakfast recipes|servings=1|time=15 minutes|difficulty=2|image=[[Image:Oatmealraisins2.jpg|300px|Oatmeal with raisins]]}}
__NOTOC__
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian]] | [[Cookbook:Breakfast|Breakfast]]

'''Porridge''' (also known in American English as '''hot cereal'''), is a simple dish made by boiling [[Cookbook:Grain|grain]] (often [[Cookbook:Rolled Oats|rolled oats]]) in water or milk. Porridge made from Irish oats, also called steel-cut oats, takes longer to cook—typically 15–20 minutes.

==Ingredients==
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (45 [[Cookbook:gram|g]]) rolled [[Cookbook:Oats|oats]] or other grain
* ¾ cup (180 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) water
* ¾ cup (180 ml) [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]]

==Procedure==
#Mix oats and water, then bring to the [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], covered with a lid.
#Once bubbling, stir and reduce temperature to the lowest possible to maintain [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmering]]. Replace lid and watch carefully to prevent boiling over.
#Stir every minute or so. After five minutes, remove lid, stir thoroughly and add milk.
#Mix through, and keep stirring until fully mixed.
#Serve and add [[cookbook:raisin|raisins]], [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]], [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]], [[Cookbook:Maple Syrup|maple syrup]], a pinch of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]], [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]] or inverted sugar syrup to taste.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* Soak whole grains over night and change water. Soaking softens the grains and reduces cooking time, although whole oats still require 45–60 minutes simmering. Rinsing also reduces starch and pesticide residue. Steel cut oats should simmer for 20–30 minutes, or to the desired texture. Let the water boil out for a chewier, rice-like flavor with whole oats or leave some water in as is common with rolled oats and instant oats.
* Porridge can be made using water, milk, or a mixing of the two depending on taste. Other ingredients may include [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], [[Cookbook:Date|dates]], [[Cookbook:Banana|bananas]], [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]], and [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]. Add apples and cinnamon during the cooking process to infuse the flavor. If you want to avoid milk products, it is also possible to use [[Cookbook:Soy Milk|soy milk]] instead of cow's milk. Corn oil also works well with honey and figs, out of the vegetable oils. Honey itself combines well with apples and cinnamon while raisins, dates, and bananas are popular with dairy ingredients. Winter squash can be added to finer grains like wheat and millet.
* 3 tbsp (90 ml) of milk powder or non-dairy milk powder can replace liquid milk by increasing water to 1½ cups (360 ml)
* Porridge was traditionally cooked over a wooden fire and in a cast iron pot which prevents burning and doesn't interfere with the flavor. In modern times, any pot will do as long as it is thick enough to distribute the heat. 
* Instant oats are the easiest and fastest to cook as they only need boiling water and as this may be also done with a microwave oven.

title: Cookbook:Nigerian Tomato Omelette
text:
{{Recipe summary
| Category = Egg recipes
| Difficulty = 2
| Image = [[File:Omelette with butter and tomatoes.jpg|300px]]
}}

{{Recipe}}

'''Nigerian tomato omelette''' is a simple dish of egg and tomato.

== Ingredients ==

* [[Cookbook:Egg|Eggs]]
* [[Cookbook:Tomato|Tomatoes]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]]

== Equipment ==

* [[Cookbook:Stovetop|Stove]]
* [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]]
* [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|Frying pan]]
* Bowls
* [[Cookbook:Spatula|Spatula]]

== Procedure ==

# Heat some oil in a pan over high heat. Add the tomatoes, and fry until well-heated. 
# [[Cookbook:Mixing|Beat]] the eggs, and stir in the cooked tomato. Return the mixture to the pan over medium-low heat, making sure it is evenly spread across the pan. Cook until the egg is sturdy enough to flip.
# Flip the omelette to the other side, and cook until the bottom is golden.
# Serve hot with bread or jollof rice.
